findings.title: S-8 still exempts GND at the PYRO1_OUT barrels, the one inner neighbour that bypasses Q124 and fires an enabled match; the OUT via barrel is 0.251 mm from In1 GND and from In2 GND

evidence.reference: PYRO1_OUT via (11.630, 55.100), 0.5 mm ring / 0.3 mm drill, no inner pads; J121.1 (7.400, 54.100), 1.3 mm hole, 1.9 mm ring flashed on In1 and In2; Q124.5 drain; tools/check_r10.py at acba196 lines 868-874 (BARREL_GND_HAZARD = {ACT_GATE, ACT_DRV})
evidence.measured: OUT via barrel wall to GND: 0.251 mm on In1 and 0.251 mm on In2. J121.1 hole wall to GND 0.550 mm on In1 and In2; its own inner ring to GND 0.250 mm. The same numbers come from three independent routes: pcbnew 10.0.7 geometry export + own numpy distances (s8_own_a3144b15.txt), the fabricated In1/In2 Gerbers parsed with their X2 net attributes (gerber_s8.json), and the committed check_r10.s8 re-run with GND counted for every barrel net (committed_s8.txt: 0.251 / 0.551 mm). As shipped, S-8 passes because GND is exempt for PYRO1_OUT.
evidence.rationale_text: check_r10.py comment: 'GND on the N-FET gate, the enable chain (...) or the pyro bus nodes holds them off'. For PYRO1_OUT this is wrong: OUT is Q124's drain, so OUT-GND bypasses Q124. R10_VALIDATION section 1 itself says 'An OUT-to-GND bridge or failed-short Q124 can fire an enabled match' and also 'GND is permitted for the four original barrels'.
evidence.calculation: With the bus enabled, OUT shorted to GND leaves the F7 fire loop (4.618 ohm native allocation) intact except Q124's RDS(on): about 1.5 A at the 7.4 V-equivalent source, above the 1.125 A floor and the J-Tek 0.75 A all-fire (REQUIREMENTS F7 and Igniters row).

findings.impact: From the on-rail bus enable until apogee, one inner-layer short or CAF path at either OUT barrel fires the e-match. It cannot be inspected, coated or reworked. A static short is caught by the passive cold screen (CONT and BUS both near 0 V against 96/96 mV healthy; Calculation, sense_cases.txt), so it needs a defect that forms or becomes intermittent inside the armed window. This is the same 0.25 mm inner geometry that R18-SAF-01 / D-R18-04 cleared to 1.05 mm at the ACT_GATE barrels, where one fault only removes the first of two barriers; here it is the last barrier. The gate's stated reason for exempting GND is factually wrong for this net.
findings.concrete_fix: (1) tools/check_r10.py: BARREL_GND_HAZARD = {'ACT_GATE', 'ACT_DRV', 'PYRO1_OUT'} and correct the comment. (2) r10_route_ground.barrel_keepouts: add PYRO1_OUT barrels on In1 and In2, radius drill/2 + 1.05 mm: 1.20 mm round (11.630, 55.100) and 1.70 mm round J121.1 (7.400, 54.100) (2.00 mm if J121.1 keeps its inner ring, see R19-SAF-05). (3) Add PYRO1_OUT to critical_reference.R10_SLOW_RETURN_NETS (a DC fire/sense net) or exempt barrel keep-out voids in K-region / K-reference, because the OUT F.Cu and B.Cu tracks leaving the via and J121.1 cross the new voids. Checked: the GND partner via (10.300, 55.600) barrel edge is 1.271 mm from the OUT via centre, outside the 1.20 mm disc; its flashed In1/In2 ring then sits 1.021 mm from the OUT barrel. No other GND via or inner track lies inside either disc; the 1.42 mm partner-via distance is unchanged. Alternative without CAD: record the inner OUT-GND gaps explicitly as an accepted instance of the OUT-GND class and correct the gate comment.

findings.title: Pad-arming switch J400: four neighbours of U9's high-impedance EN node within 0.2-0.33 mm, plus the J400.2 lead, can bypass or latch the switch. They are unrecorded, or recorded as fail-safe. The EN network is uncoated, and no per-flight step shows that J400 still turns the board off

evidence.file: m3_design/assembly_review/m3.kicad_pcb; docs/ORDERING.md section 8.3 / 8.4 and docs/M3_R10.md at acba196; m3_design/assembly_review/sources/r10_design/R10_DECISIONS.md D-R18-03
evidence.reference: EN node BAT_ENABLE: U9.1 B(17.600, 82.300); R81 300 kohm to GND, R80 + R165 = 940 kohm from BAT_IN through J400 when closed; C87 2.2 uF
evidence.measured: (a) U9.1 (EN) to U9.5 (IN, BAT_IN) and to the BAT_IN feed track (18.250, 81.600)-(18.250, 83.400): 0.200 mm, B.Cu, under the QFN body. (b) BAT_ENABLE via (17.100, 82.800) to the BAT_FAULT_N F.Cu L (16.550, 80.900)-(16.550, 83.350)-(19.300, 83.350): 0.200 mm. (c) BAT_ENABLE via (19.675, 66.400) to R134.2 (RAW_ACT, bare 2512 pad): 0.300 mm, B.Cu. (d) R123.1 (ACT_EN) to the BAT_ENABLE F.Cu track (21.300, 68.900)-(21.300, 75.200): 0.330 mm. Inventory: adjacency_a3144b15.json.
evidence.calculation: Thresholds (TPS25947 VUVLO rising 1.183-1.223 V, falling 1.076-1.116 V): (a) switch bypass, board on with J400 open, for a leak <= 1.52-1.83 Mohm from BAT_IN (7.4-8.4 V). (b) Once the board is on, BAT_FAULT_N (R89 10 kohm to 3V3) holds EN at 3.3 x 300/310 = 3.19 V, so J400 cannot turn it off; latch for a leak <= 0.58 Mohm. (c) Once PC1 has enabled the bus, RAW_ACT holds EN on; latch for a leak <= 1.69-1.96 Mohm. (d) D-R18-03 / M3_R10 say a bridge 'loads U9's 470 kohm-fed EN with 2 kohm, so U9 stays off'. That is true only while PC1 is low. With PC1 high, ACT_EN is 2.2 V through 667 ohm, so EN stays at about 2.2 V and J400 cannot turn the board off (leak <= 0.29 Mohm). Hard bridges (b)-(d) present at power-up stop the board starting (EN loaded by 10 kohm / 11.2 kohm / 2 kohm), so they are self-revealing. They defeat the switch only if they form, or conduct (moisture, unwashed flux; ORDERING asks JLC for no washing), after power-up. Harness: the J400.2 lead (BAT_SW_RETURN, at EN potential) touching any pack-voltage conductor (the J1.1 lead, servo pack-star +) gives EN = 7.4 x 300/770 = 2.88 V, i.e. the board is on with the switch open.
evidence.records: ORDERING 8.3 coating worksheet selects R123's cell but not U9, R80, R81, R165, C87 or the BAT_ENABLE vias and tracks. The per-flight check (ORDERING 8.3, R10_VEHICLE_HANDOFF) measures J121.2 with J400 open, so it sees only a live bus, never a board that is on, and never exercises switch-off. The 20 switch cycles with 3V3 < 0.3 V are a first-article step. ORDERING 8.4 dresses only battery and igniter leads apart. The battery_entry note treats a chafed SW lead only as EN over-voltage. R8_VALIDATION recorded this 'BAT_ENABLE latch class' for R8; R10's section 1 carries only the inner-layer case (R18-SAF-01) and ACT_EN as fail-safe.
evidence.maker: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps25947.pdf (SLVSFC9C, rev. May 2026) p9 (VUVLO(R) 1.183/1.20/1.223 V, VUVLO(F) 1.076/1.09/1.116 V, IENLKG +/-0.1 uA), p5 (EN/UVLO pin)

findings.impact: J400 is the sole power and pad-arming device, and 'off first' is the safing step. A single surface leak or bridge at these sites, or one chafe of the J400.2 lead, can leave the board powered with the bus enabled after the crew opens the switch. Q124 and the firmware are then the only barriers while people are at the rocket. This never fires by itself.
findings.concrete_fix: CAD (fix-now): move the BAT_ENABLE via (19.675, 66.400) to (19.675, 66.600); F.Cu stub (19.675, 66.000)-(19.675, 66.600); B.Cu (19.675, 66.600)-(21.000, 67.925)-(21.000, 68.600). Checked against all fixed copper (pours re-flow): via ring to R134.2 0.300 -> 0.500 mm; the new segments are >= 0.425 mm from every other net; the GND partner via (20.706, 65.619) stays 1.42 mm centre to centre; the In2 keep-out follows the via. BAT_FAULT_N corner at (17.1, 82.8): no clean shift found, because x = 16.25 hits C96.2 (0.10 mm) and D9.2 (0.10 mm); record it instead. Records: add the four pairs and their leak thresholds to deviation section 1, and correct the D-R18-03 / M3_R10 'U9 stays off' wording. Coating: add U9, R80, R81, R165, C87 and the BAT_ENABLE vias and tracks. Procedure, per flight before the e-match goes in: with the pack connected and J400 open, confirm the board is off (no telemetry or buzzer, or 3V3 / TP81 < 0.3 V). After any closed-switch check, confirm that opening J400 turns it off. Harness: run the J400 pair twisted, on its own ties, away from the battery and servo power leads. Respin option: divide the EN network impedance by 10 (C87 x 10 keeps the bounce timing) to raise every leak threshold tenfold; this also helps the 7 uA dry contact.

findings.title: Side effect of D-R18-02: TP121's new 7.14 mm B.Cu stub doubles the ACT_GATE copper at the 0.25 mm pour clearance from GND, and adds an ACT_GATE to BAT_SW_SOURCE pair at 0.400 mm

evidence.measured: ACT_GATE track length within 0.30 mm of GND copper (sampled every 0.05 mm, act_gate_exposure.txt): 6.277 mm on 632a9ad3 -> 12.872 mm on a3144b15, of which the stub is 5.243 mm. The stub is 0.400 mm from the BAT_SW_SOURCE via; that pair did not exist on 632a9ad3 (adjacency diff). The stub is 1.300 mm from J400.2.
evidence.calculation: Stub to GND bridge: VGS of Q120/Q121 about -6.8 V with J400 open, so the bus goes live (the per-flight J121.2 check catches it if it exists before the e-match goes in). Stub to BAT_SW_SOURCE bridge: with J400 closed and PC1 high, ACT_GATE is about 1.2 V, so EN is about 1.2 x 300/770 = 0.47 V and U9 turns off; the board resets at every bus enable (fail-safe, detectable). With J400 open the bridge has no effect.
evidence.records: ORDERING 8.3: TP121 is 'coated with its cell', so after coating it is not a probe. R119.1 B(11.14, 71.1) and C120.2 B(17.1, 73.3) are bare ACT_GATE pads in the same cell for pre-coating measurement.

findings.impact: The surface instance of R18-SAF-01's hazard (ACT_GATE to GND turns the series pair on with the switch open) grew 2.05x. Both sides are masked and the stub is coated, so the probability stays low. No function needs the stub.
findings.concrete_fix: Fix-now: delete TP121 (r10_place.tsv row 'TP121 4 70 0 B'), its schematic symbol and the B.Cu segment (11.140, 70.000)-(4.000, 70.000) (r10_route_pyro.py: t('ACT_GATE','B',P,[(11.14,70.0),p('TP121.1')])). Drop TP121.1 from check_actuators.ACT_NETS and from the ORDERING / handoff probe tables, and name R119.1 or C120.2 as the ACT_GATE probe point. Result: 12.872 -> 7.629 mm at the pour clearance, and no ACT_GATE to BAT_SW_SOURCE pair.

evidence.measured: 49 protected/foreign outer-layer net-pair rows within 0.5 mm (27 without GND), minimum 0.173 mm (R129.1 MID to GND via (22.330, 58.250)). Unrecorded consequence-bearing pairs: R134.2 (RAW_ACT, (19.075, 64.000)) to GND via (20.706, 65.619), 0.196 mm; this is R81.2's fan-out via, and R81.2 already joins the F.Cu GND fill. The RAW_ACT feed (14.475, 67.105)-(17.580, 64.000), 0.5 mm wide, runs under R134's body 0.367 mm from R134.1 (IGN). The RAW_ACT sense branch (22.800, 61.400)-(22.800, 63.875) is 0.175 mm from the USB_OVLO track (22.500, 64.250)-(23.500, 64.250) and 0.225 mm from R87.1 (USB_LIMITED). The MID corridor is 0.250 mm from R134.2.
evidence.calculation: R134.2 to GND with the bus enabled: the pack is shorted through Q120/Q121 without R134, the match or its leads, about 23 A (7.4 V over the ~0.32 ohm left of the 4.62 ohm F7 loop; unfused) until BAT_IN sag resets the logic. R134.1 to RAW_ACT removes R134 (about 12 A into a match that shorts after firing, instead of 4.2 A). RAW_ACT to USB_OVLO puts 7.4-8.4 V on U11.5 OV2, above its 6 V absolute maximum. RAW_ACT to R87.1 puts USB 5 V on the bus with PC1 low whenever USB is attached; the procedure forbids an e-match with USB. MID to RAW_ACT (sense_cases.txt): cold screen with an open match reads CONT/BUS 102.0 / 55.5 mV, against healthy 96.2 / 96.1 and open 141.5 / 0.0 mV; the powered CONT is 1.213 V at 7.4 V whether the match is open or intact. D-R18-05 says only that an upper bound can flag the bridge.

findings.impact: The owner is asked to accept a surface-fault list that belongs to older copper. With the MID bridge, continuity detection depends on firmware bands for both CONT and BUS, not on a CONT upper bound alone. None of these pairs fires the match by itself.
findings.concrete_fix: Replace the stale count in deviation section 1 with the current inventory (this review's JSON rows), stating each consequence above, and extend D-R18-05's residual text with the open-match masking case and the need for a BUS lower band in the cold screen. Optional CAD: re-space the RAW_ACT sense branch from USB_OVLO and R87 (it can leave R134.2 northward before x = 21.5).

findings.title: S-8 measures from the hole wall and ignores the protected THT pads' own 1.9 mm inner rings: on In2, J400.2 to RAW_PROTECTED is 0.750 mm and J121.1 to 3V3 is 0.803 mm copper to copper, while the deviation list reports +0.050 / +0.103 mm over the 1.0 mm floor

AP63203 runs PFM and does not sink current (Inference), so 3V3 rises toward the SRV05-4 clamp while the match carries roughly 0.3-0.8 A, against the J-Tek 0.30 A no-fire and 0.75 A all-fire (Calculation/Inference). coverage_limits: No firmware exists. The screen bands, the PC1 policy and switch-off annunciation are procedure statements, not executed code.
No bench, transient, leakage, CAF or ESD testing. Leak thresholds are static calculations against TPS25947 limits; the 3V3 back-drive current is an estimate (PFM non-sinking is Inference).
Fabricated hole size, registration and plating were not allocated (deviation row 9 stays open). Distances are nominal CAD values.
Surface pairs involving a tented via or a masked track need a mask breach to bridge. Probabilities are not quantified.
Inventory limited to 15 pyro / arming nets (outer < 0.5 mm, inner < 1.0 mm). Other nets were not swept. Double faults were only spot-checked.
Candidate CAD changes were checked against fixed copper only (pours assumed to re-flow); not built, not run through route_check or the full gate.
Datasheets are the cached maker PDFs listed; the MJG no-fire figure comes from the project record.
Other agents were editing docs, tools and the fab outputs in the worktree during the review; every quoted record and every fab file is the committed acba196 version.
No other round19 report or .supervisor/r19_* directory was opened.
